classification_legend.proved_for_required_scope: Observed assertions/evidence satisfy this gate within the expressly stated fixture and platform scope.
classification_legend.partial: There is relevant passing evidence, but at least one explicit part or required breadth remains unproved.
classification_legend.incomplete: A required acceptance branch is missing, failed, or deliberately unavailable.
classification_legend.unverified: No adequate executed evidence establishes the gate.

gates.requirement: A01-A63 each have automated or repeatable acceptance evidence.
evidence: All six audits cover 63 unique A01-A63 rows, with no missing or open classifications; referenced test functions exist.

gates.requirement: A fresh supported Agent session bootstraps correctly before its first project mutation.

The later exclusive-MCP A35 record docs/claude-mcp-auth-second-evidence.json proves owned resume and a typed auth diagnostic, but explicitly fails the full workflow because readonly inspection before resume was not proved. The earlier MCP attempt also failed its reads.
docs/claude-mcp-auth-evidence.json proves the latest readonly A35 auth handoff: canonical read, inspect, typed diagnostic, external-login-only request, unchanged free owner and context privacy.

docs/remaining-gates-review.json confirms historical Codex/Claude first-mutation evidence meets the quoted scenario, without an invented every-profile replay condition. The later A54 review found those native-tool launch paths still expose private-root; they now fail closed before model execution.

docs/feature-workflow-evidence.json records an independently authorized Haiku 5.5 exclusive-MCP feature turn: canonical read, inspection, owned resume, conditional managed app.py mutation, preserved source/index/mainline/owner and absent context capability. gates.requirement: Takeover and publication-integrity decisions have stale-decision tests.
evidence: tests/test_publication.py::test_stale_decision asserts code 3, stale decision lifecycle, no push, and unchanged post-release ref/owner/private trust/source state when an older takeover decision is applied.
tests/test_integrity_records.py stale integrity decision coverage changes the remote HEAD after proposal and verifies the stale choice is rejected without publication or local-state mutation.
gaps: The tests establish local runtime behavior; they do not claim every hosting transport or provider scenario.

gates.requirement: Project semantic conflicts do not enter the runtime decision engine.
evidence: tests/test_decisions.py::test_A32_A33_project_semantics_cannot_enter_runtime_decisions exercises test-bug/product-feature categories and verifies they are not runtime decision choices or mutations.
gaps: This is a local category-boundary test; no broader fresh-agent UX claim is made because §25.8 does not require one.
gates.next_step: Preserve this separation; do not add product/test semantics to runtime decision categories.

gates.requirement: Host installation/recovery tests prove no arbitrary damage to existing VPN, network, SSH, or provider configuration.
evidence: tests/test_host_guard.py and docs/host-preservation.md exercise selected Linux configuration paths and fail-closed inspection.

docs/installer-repair-evidence.json records one isolated Linux prefix launcher repair with verified healthy and pre-repair backups, only the approved launcher content repaired, and unrelated prefix entries preserved; no comprehensive global host snapshot was performed.

Primary reviewed docs/remaining-gates-review.json against exact §25.9: named selected VPN/network/SSH/provider categories preserved in actual install/recovery tests. Full Windows/live-service/global-state certification is not demanded by this gate.
gaps: Selected Linux configuration/isolated repair scope only; future changes that touch broader §5.2 categories require scoped guards.
gates.next_step: Preserve existing guarded minimum-change installer/recovery behavior; no broader snapshot is required for the current isolated operations.

gates.requirement: Unsupported provider/platform/backend paths fail closed or are explicitly marked unsupported; there is no silent safety downgrade.
evidence: Basic Doppler mode explicitly reports no strong provider fencing/conditional-write/terminal capability; user-approved simpler contract documented, not a silent downgrade.
docs/provider-tool-isolation-design.md and the Landlock evidence explicitly limit the sandbox and deny unsupported execution rather than claiming network or full filesystem isolation.

docs/support-capability-matrix.md and tests/test_git_unsupported_boundaries.py record actual SHA256/Gitlink/root-and-nested-LFS rejections plus adversarial pre-push/fsmonitor controls; profile tests reject canonicalModel mismatch.
README and support matrix distinguish Python>=3.12 installation floor from verified Python3.12. Unrestricted provider smoke constructors now fail closed; no unsafe fallback.
gaps: Native Windows/macOS, SHA256 repositories, submodules/LFS and unsafe native-tool profiles remain unsupported as documented.
gates.next_step: Keep supported/unsupported boundaries explicit; do not substitute disabled required features for v1.2 completion.

acceptance_scope.coverage: A01-A63, indexed by six requirement-level audits
important_scope_limits: Local/fake-provider evidence does not prove Doppler write fencing or terminal behavior.
Historical successful A59 sessions and the A63 missing-secret stop are scenario-specific, not universal provider evidence.
A58 is one isolated Linux launcher repair; it is not a full host-configuration preservation certificate.

decision: Verified implementation baseline for the explicitly approved basic Doppler contract on the documented Ubuntu/WSL scope. All ten gates have scoped evidence; historical failures and unsupported boundaries remain retained.
scope_amendment: User approved basic Doppler writes/current-state confirmation. Strong provider CAS/fencing/terminal API requirements are superseded.
